title: Varna 3. The Description of the Childhood Pastimes and the Upanayana
html:
The infant Jagadisha repeats Krishna's name from his first words, plays at sankirtana with the neighbours' children and worships a clay form of Krishna; his parents recognize in him an associate of the Lord; the "chalk in the hand" rite, a prayer to Krishna for bhakti, mastery of all the shastras and of the "Bhagavata" by the age of eight; the upanayana in his ninth year; praise of Jagadisha's mercy and the author's signature

The third varna

1Him who in childhood, while still speaking half-words, [showed] the power of the japa of Krishna's name — that Srimad Jagadisha of wondrous deeds I worship.1

2Glory, glory to Jagadisha, the ocean of mercy!
Show mercy, Prabhu: I am very wretched.

3When in childhood the Prabhu's speech began to come,
he took to uttering constantly the names of Radha and Krishna.

4Babbling half-words, he utters the sweetest name of Krishna;
hearing [this], Bhagyavati Devi was filled with abundant joy.

5Calling Kamalaksha, the chaste lady in great bliss says:
"Your son is by no means an ordinary man.

6From the child's mouth come words of Krishna all the time;
he is an associate of the Lord — this I have understood fully.

7When he is hungry, he always says, 'Krishna, Krishna';
even as he falls asleep, [his] tongue takes the name of Krishna.

8Saying 'Krishna, Krishna, Krishna!' he weeps;
and at times, hearing the name of Krishna, he stops crying.

9Hearing the name of Krishna, his face breaks into smiles;
in the bliss of Krishna's name at times he dances.

10He calls many sons of the neighbouring twice-born
and constantly plays the game of Krishna-sankirtana.

11Out of clay he shapes an image (murti) of Krishna
and worships it with various forest flowers.

12Taking sweets and other food from me,
he steadies his mind and offers [them] to Krishna.

13Thus day and night he abides in feeling for Krishna.
Know for certain: he is one of the Lord's associates."

14Hearing this, the Bandya says to her: "Listen, wife:
I know that [our] son is an associate of the Lord.

15Raise him with care;
by this we both shall attain the goal of life."

16Thus the two, with great joy at heart,
raise their son day and night.

17I bow down at the feet of these two,
whose son is my Prabhu Jagadisha.

18The childhood pastimes of Sri Jagadisha, as if in a sutra,
for my own purification I describe briefly.

19When the Prabhu reached the age of five years,
his father, choosing an auspicious day, placed chalk in his hand.2

20Remembering Sri Krishna, he began his learning;
by the sixth month the Prabhu had mastered writing.

21Then, after some days, the Prabhu began his reading;
[but] he gave his mind to the lotus feet of Sri Krishna.

22At his father's insistence he writes and reads,
but this becomes an obstacle to remembering Krishna's feet.

23Pained by the obstacles to his bhajana,
the Prabhu prays thus to the feet of Sri Krishna:

24"Lord, by Your mercy always arrange this:
that I may give up maya and worship Your feet.

25Do not bind me with the maya of worldly things;
do not deceive me, Lord, by giving me various kinds of learning."

26Thus he always worships Krishna;
staying near his guru, he does not study.

27[Yet] when the guru asks about the lesson,
by Krishna's mercy he recites all that [was to be] learned.

28Grammar, lexicons, literature, drama,
alankara, smriti, nyaya, the darshanas, "sulyaka",3

29the agamas, the nigamas — and he also studied Vedanta;
a knower of all the shastras, no one finds the limit of his [learning].

30The four Vedas and fourteen shastras he learned as if in play;4
all the ancient Puranas and the rest he read.

31Having thus studied various books,
at last he reads the Srimad Bhagavata.

32In it he found the highest message of the truth about Krishna;
on the reading of that book the Prabhu fixed his mind.

33Regarding the book as Krishna's own form, he worships it;5
in the Prabhu's heart there is no thought of other books.

34Thus Jagadisha accomplished all [this]:
in his eighth year he completed his studies.

35Taking his guru's leave, he came to his own home
and with full ceremony bowed at the feet of his father and mother.

36Looking at their son's face, both rejoice at heart;
taking the son on their laps, they kiss [him] with affection.

37Bringing various sweets, they placed them beside their son;
seeing the excellent food, the Prabhu was glad.

38With a happy mind he offers [it] to Sri Krishna;
Krishna's prasada he gave first to his mother.

39A little at a time he distributed it to other people,
and he himself ate a little of the maha-prasada.

40Seeing his son's conduct, Kamalaksha Bandya
together with his own people became greatly joyful.

41When the son reached the age of nine years,
[his father] resolved in his mind: "Now I shall give him the sacred thread."

42Gathering his own kinsfolk, he fixed the day;
the brahmana set about collecting all that was needed.

43For Jagadisha's auspicious rite, by Krishna's mercy,6
from who knows where the things needed came and presented themselves.

44Thus provisions of many kinds were gathered;
he invited all his relatives and kinsmen by marriage.

45He invited brahmanas from various lands;
all of them came on the day of the upanayana.

46The brahmanas came and assembled;
Jagadisha received the sacred thread.

47Everyone was treated to various dishes;
Kamalaksha gratified everyone as befitted each.

48How the Prabhu's upanayana took place
I have written briefly, fearing to make the book too long.

49The Prabhu, wearing the sacred thread, displayed such sweetness —
seeing it, the eyes are soothed.
Whoever sees that loveliness becomes free of worldly attachment
and without effort attains Krishna's feet.

50Whoever worships those feet is a supreme devotee;
there is none as fortunate as he.
Jagadisha, by the power of mercy, wandering through Gauda-mandala,
gives bhakti to anyone and everyone.

51Setting aside all the shastras, describing the greatness of bhakti,
he made the living beings take up bhakti to Krishna.
Thus all the living beings, becoming followers of the Prabhu,
obtained the strength for the bhajana of Krishna.

52One to whom Jagadisha is merciful crosses [the ocean of] existence with ease;
Vrindavana becomes attainable for him.
Therefore I say: by no means fall into the delusion of worldly things —
take the shelter of his feet.

53Worship those lotus feet — these bonds of existence will fall away;
have no doubt at all about this.
By the power of those feet you will cross the ocean of maya —
know these words as certain.

54All the virtues of Jagadisha — to set them down in a book
I have no such power.
The mind bound up in worldly things is not still for a moment;
at all times it is seized by maya.

55Wickedness is maya's nature: she has made [me] take up a wicked dharma;
she raises opposition on the path of bhakti.
O mind, be attentive: maya is very powerful —
[beware] lest she ever drown [you].7

56Binding my mind to Jagadisha's lotus feet,
casting away every other hope,
being happy myself, to write the Prabhu's virtues in a book —
this became my desire.

57When such was my mind, in a dream a command was given
by my Prabhu Bhagavatananda.
In accordance with that Prabhu's order, the life of Jagadisha
was composed by this Ananda Dasa.

Thus in the Charitra-vijaya of Sri Jagadisha Pandita ends the third varna, called "The Description of the Childhood Pastimes and the Upanayana".

Notes

  1. The edition's text of the shloka: «যো বাল্যে বচনার্দ্ধোক্তৌ কৃষ্ণ নাম জপা বলং। তং চিত্ররচিতং শ্রীমজ্জগদীশং ভজাম্যহং ॥». The grammar of the first line is unclear: «জপা বলং» (japā balaṁ) is taken as "the power of japa"; «চিত্ররচিতং» (citra-racitaṁ, "wondrously composed/adorned") is taken as «চিত্রচরিতং» (citra-caritaṁ), "of wondrous deeds".
  2. Hate-khari (হাতে খড়ি, "chalk in the hand") — the rite that begins a child's education: chalk is placed in the child's hand, and he traces his first letters.
  3. «সুল্যক» — the reading is unclear and the word is not identified; possibly a corrupted name of one more discipline.
  4. The fourteen shastras (caturdaśa vidyā) — by the traditional count, the four Vedas, the six Vedangas, the Puranas, nyaya, mimamsa and the dharma-shastras.
  5. Cf. Bhagavata, 1.3.43: this Purana, shining like the sun, has arisen now that Krishna has departed to His own abode.
  6. The edition reads «শুভ বর্ণে» (śubha varṇe); taken as "in the auspicious rite" — possibly «শুভ কর্মে» (śubha karme). In the edition the first line of the couplet ends with «॥» instead of «।».
  7. The edition reads «নাড়ু বায়» (nāṛu bāy); taken as «না ডুবায়» (nā ḍubāy), "lest she drown".
